A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same P3O work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. The relocated references and reformatted appendices can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original simulation results on pendulum, cart-pole, light-dark, and triangulation tasks, including learning curves and learned trajectory examples.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional LQG validation, gradient-variance measurements, and particle-count and temperature sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The Feynman–Kac objective, policy-gradient estimator, nested particle filters, optional backward sampling, and policy architectures are retained in Algorithms 1–2 and Appendices C–D. Formula corrections and clarified Gaussian notation do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds a two-dimensional linear-Gaussian system with quadratic rewards for the tractable LQG experiment. The four original tasks remain; the particle-count and temperature studies reuse cart-pole and light-dark.

E2.justification: The closed-form LQG solution becomes a new evaluated comparator in v2 Figure 1. SLAC, DVRL, and DualSMC remain in the corresponding four-task comparison, moved from v1 Figure 1 to v2 Figure 2.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands the evaluation design with controlled particle-count and temperature sweeps and a gradient-covariance metric. For example, Figure 4 varies cart-pole belief particles over 32, 128, and 512 while fixing history particles at 256. The original benchmark metric, 1024 evaluation rollouts, and default particle counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 contains trajectory case studies but no hyperparameter sweeps. v2 adds analyses of how inner and outer particle counts affect learning, how temperature affects convergence, and how temperature affects gradient variance (Figures 1, 4, and 5). These directly examine previously untested properties of P3O.

E5.justification: v2 first quantifies policy-gradient variability through the covariance trace plotted against temperature in Figure 1. The original return-reporting practice—means and standard errors over 10 training seeds—is retained and also used in Figure 4. No increase in the original experiments' run counts is stated.

E6.justification: New results show P3O approaching the LQG reference, decreasing gradient variance with increasing temperature, and particle-budget and temperature effects on learning. Figures 4–5 add substantial sensitivity results, including diminishing returns from additional particles. The original four-task learning curves are unchanged after renumbering.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the predictive-observation approximation by removing an extra summation and transition-density factor, leaving a weighted observation-likelihood mixture. The main propositions and proofs remain intact. Appendix B largely reformulates the existing Bellman equations using histories instead of belief-state notation.

C1.justification: The abstract changes its explicit stated advantage from avoiding extrinsic exploration bonuses to avoiding suboptimal approximations. This is a limited reframing; the three contribution bullets and the central claim of deliberate information gathering remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges unquantified bias in the nested estimator, elaborates high-dimensional proposal mismatch and temperature-related bias/degeneracy, and recommends avoiding backward sampling for long horizons. Some task discussions stop explicitly crediting DVRL, although its benchmark curves and the shared caption remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a specific GitHub code URL instead of referring only to supplementary code and clarifies the diagonal Gaussian action distribution. However, Appendix D.2 removes the explicit mini-batch size of 16 trajectories and eight updates per SMC run, retaining only unspecified mini-batches and multiple updates.

R1.justification: v2 adds Doucet et al. (2000), Guarniero et al. (2017), and Naesseth et al. (2018) when discussing improved particle proposals, and removes Puterman (2014). The central positioning against QMDP-based approaches and other POMDP solvers is largely retained.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized explanatory and language edits, rewrites Appendix B around history-based notation, shortens the conclusion, and moves references before the appendices. Author affiliations and conference-header text also change. Most of the main exposition and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the graphical presentation with the two-panel LQG/variance figure, four-panel particle-count figure, and two-panel temperature figure. The original benchmark and trajectory displays become Figures 2–3, with the trajectory graphic reformatted. Architecture Tables 1–4 retain their structure and contents.

improvement.justification: The LQG reference and particle/temperature studies strengthen validation and characterize sensitivities that v1 left unexamined, within the same low-dimensional scope. More explicit bias limitations and a direct code pointer improve transparency. These gains are partly offset by removing exact mini-batch and update-count details; the core method, proofs, and original benchmark evidence remain largely stable.
